justification: Three commits, each already carrying its own Standard-tier QA in its commit message, had never had a per-branch report generated — the branch-level artifact this repo's gate actually resolves on push. This file consolidates those three without re-deriving anything: (1) 26f9dd82 wires instrument_registry.legislation_url as a citation fallback for 35 documents with no r2_pdf_url/source_url; (2) ad1249a3 recovers 54 stale dcp_setback_controls citation links via a hand-verified chapter_key alias map; (3) 786fb4a7 fixes a bare-apex origin fallback across 14 stripe/report route files. No served value changes beyond what each commit's own QA already pinned; no schema, no migration, no production write.

falsifiable_check.command: cd frontend-nextjs && npx jest __tests__/lib/citation-instrument-urls.test.ts __tests__/app-links-use-verify-subdomain.test.ts && cd .. && python -m pytest tests/test_conveyancing_chapter_key_aliases.py -v
falsifiable_check.fails_when: resolveCitationUrl's priority order (image > chapter > instrument > null) breaks, a CHAPTER_KEY_ALIASES entry stops resolving or overwrites a key the registry already resolved directly, or a stripe/report route reverts to the bare-apex fallback string.
falsifiable_check.observed_red: Each commit force-reverted its own fix and confirmed the specific test failed at the specific file:line before restoring: citation-instrument-urls (35 matched ids resolve / 17 unmatched proven absent), chapter_key aliases (highest-value entry, 15 of 54 rows, reverted -> red), bare-apex fallback (one file reverted to the old default -> app-links-use-verify-subdomain.test.ts's new BARE_APEX_FALLBACK regex failed on that file:line). All three restored and green: jest 95 suites/1332 tests, tsc clean, test_conveyancing_db.py 88 tests green.

pre_impl.existing_data: documents.r2_pdf_url/source_url (35 null rows resolved via instrument_registry.legislation_url by deterministic name-derivation, re-verified against the live table, not fuzzy-matched); dcp_setback_controls.source_chapter_key (234 of 967 served rows had no working URL; 54 recovered via 24 hand-verified renames); NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL (was correctly set in Vercel, but 14 files still carried a dead bare-apex string as their code-level fallback default).
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: The alias map deliberately does NOT cover thin registries (the_hills: 1 registered chapter against 4+ referenced; camden's parking chapter unregistered at all) or ambiguous multi-candidate keys (canterbury_bankstown's bare 'ch5', ku_ring_gai's bare 'section-a') or precinct splits with no registry counterpart (leichhardt balmain/birchgrove) — guessing any of these risks citing the wrong council's document, the exact defect class this branch exists to close.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: Applies only to rows/documents with NO existing working URL; a control or document that already resolves through the existing COALESCE fallback chain is untouched by any of the three commits — proven by each commit's own forced-red test, not asserted.

functions.name: resolveCitationUrl
functions.input: a provision row (pdf_page_image_url, chapterPdfUrls lookup, document_id)
functions.output: string | null, consumed as the citation link's href
functions.if_none: falls through image -> chapter -> instrument map -> null; null renders no link, never a guessed one

functions.name: apply_chapter_key_aliases
functions.input: registry_pdf_urls dict keyed by chapter_key, CHAPTER_KEY_ALIASES constant
functions.output: same dict with aliased keys resolved before the existing COALESCE fallback runs
functions.if_none: a chapter_key with no alias entry and no direct registry match passes through unresolved, same as before this change

values.nullable: yes — a static map, absent key is the common case
values.if_missing: citation renders with no link rather than a guessed one

values.nullable: yes in a build/CI environment with no env var set
values.guard_at: the fallback default itself, corrected from the dead bare apex to the live app subdomain
values.if_missing: checkout redirect / webhook callback / shareable_url now resolves to a working app route instead of a 404

queries.purpose: confirm the 35 document ids matched to instrument_registry.legislation_url still hold given deterministic re-derivation, not a stale list
queries.file_line: re-derived against live instrument_registry per citation-instrument-urls.ts's own header comment
queries.where_clause: documents WHERE r2_pdf_url IS NULL AND source_url IS NULL, joined to instrument_registry by normalised name
queries.if_zero: no entries to add — not the case here, 35 matched
queries.if_wrong: 17 unmatched (7 SEPPs x2 naming variants + 3 non-instrument docs) proven absent, not guessed into the map

break_it.scenario: A reader treats the instrument-URL map as authoritative for every SEPP/LEP document.
break_it.what_happens: A document that later gets its own real r2_pdf_url would still resolve to the static fallback map's URL if the map is checked before the primary source.
break_it.how: resolveCitationUrl checks the per-page image and the DCP chapter URL first; the instrument map is the third-tier fallback, consulted only when both are absent.

break_it.scenario: A chapter_key alias silently overwrites a key the registry already resolves correctly.
break_it.what_happens: A working citation link would be replaced by the aliased one, potentially pointing at a different council's chapter.
break_it.how: apply_chapter_key_aliases only fills keys the registry did NOT already resolve directly — pinned by test_conveyancing_chapter_key_aliases.py.
break_it.repro: test asserts an already-resolved key is never touched by the alias map

break_it.scenario: The bare-apex fallback fix is applied to the Organization/JSON-LD identity URL, which correctly names the bare apex as the company's real site.
break_it.what_happens: A blanket host replace would turn a true statement (the company's own domain) into a false one.
break_it.how: The BARE_APEX_FALLBACK regex targets only the `?? 'https://plotdetect.com.au'` code-level default shape (a bare origin concatenated with a path later), not literal identity strings — inherited from PR #1009's narrower literal-string guard.
break_it.repro: app-links-use-verify-subdomain.test.ts distinguishes the two shapes with separate regexes
